study.title: Cerebral areas affected by unilateral acupuncture on SP3 in healthy volunteers: An explorative resting-state fMRI study
study.study_design: Within-subject crossover explorative resting-state fMRI study with pseudorandom order of effective and sham acupuncture sessions
study.randomization: Pseudorandomly assigned to order of acupuncture sessions (coin toss)
study.blinding: Sequence of acupuncture was blinded to all participants
study.population: Healthy young right-handed volunteers, 20-35 years old, seven males and eight females
study.inclusion_criteria: right-handedness; no contraindication for MRI; no history of trauma; no history of neurologic and psychiatric injury; no claustrophobia; the absence of menstruation for female subjects; no organic cerebral diseases (confirmed by routine MRI before recruitment); no addictions (e.g., smoking, drinking, and drug abuse); no drug intake within the last 7 days; no known adverse reactions to acupuncture, such as dizziness or hematoma; and range of horizontal head movement must be < 1.5 mm and < 1.5° for rotational head movement
study.exclusion_criteria: those who have the aforementioned diseases, subjects of unsuitable age (<20 or > 35 years old), and those who have limitations in head movement

arms.arm_label_exact: effective acupuncture on the SP3 point
arms.dropouts: 3 participants excluded due to head movement exceeding 1.5 mm or 1.5°
3 participants excluded due to head movement exceeding 1.5 mm or 1.5°

conditions.condition_label_exact: rs-fMRI scan after effective SP3 acupuncture

conditions.scan_context: resting-state fMRI scan (486 s) performed after effective acupuncture
resting-state fMRI scan (486 s) performed after sham acupuncture

interventions.procedure_label_exact: effective acupuncture on the right SP3 point
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: SP3 is located at the proximal end of the first metatarsophalangeal joint in the metatarsal region
interventions.needle_size_exact: 0.25 × 40 mm2; Suzhou Medical Supplies Factory Co., China
interventions.manipulation_exact: twisting angle was 180° ± 20°; needle was twisted for 20 s with 1-min interval (with needle retained)
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: yes; effective acupuncture session was performed on the right SP3 point for 15 min after getting a significant needle reaction (Deqi)
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: one session per day over two days (within-subject crossover)
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: participants were asked to remain awake and to not think about anything; questioned concerning their experience during acupuncture to confirm they were relaxed
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: SP3 point belongs to the spleen channel according to TCM meridian and collateral theory; selected unilateral acupuncture on the right side relevant to the dominant hemisphere

extraction_notes.note: Table 2 (ALFF) lists cluster rows 2 and 3 with the same brain region label (Parietal_Sup_L/R, Occipital_Sup_R, Precuneus_L) but different cluster sizes (65 and 50) and different peak coordinates and T values. These appear to be two separate clusters within the same broader anatomical grouping. Extracted as separate rows (ALFF_dec_row2 and ALFF_dec_row3) to preserve all data.

The coordinate space is not explicitly stated in the paper as MNI but the paper uses SPM12 and DPARSF with MNI standard space normalization, so MNI is strongly implied. All coordinates extracted as MNI per this inference.
Expectancy, credibility of treatment, and allocation guessing were not assessed or reported in this study. No instrument was used to measure these constructs.

No formal deqi quantification instrument (e.g., Massachusetts General Hospital Acupuncture Sensation Scale) was used. Authors acknowledge this as a limitation. Deqi was determined only by subjective participant report in traditional fashion.
No clinical or behavioral outcome measures were administered; the study was purely a neuroimaging investigation in healthy volunteers. The clinical_behavioral_outcomes section is therefore empty.

The paper states 15 participants were enrolled but 3 were excluded due to head movement, leaving n=12 for neuroimaging analysis. The arms both reflect n=15 assigned and n=12 analyzed, consistent with within-subject crossover design where the same 3 were excluded from both conditions.

The n_total_randomized field is null because the paper uses the term 'pseudorandomly' (coin toss for order assignment) rather than formal randomization with allocation concealment. This is described as an experimental design feature to avoid carry-over effects.

Adverse events were not explicitly reported in a dedicated adverse events section. The inclusion criteria required no known adverse reactions to acupuncture, and no adverse events are mentioned in results or discussion.

Table 1 (ReHo) cluster row 1 includes both BA18 (Lingual) and BA17 (Calcarine) and BA41 (Temporal_Sup_R) in the same cluster of 1886 voxels with a single peak coordinate. These are distinct anatomical regions sharing one peak. Extracted as a single row with all regions listed in brain_region_exact field.
The paper does not report the n_total_analyzed value for clinical outcomes because no clinical outcomes were assessed; all outcome data is neuroimaging-only.

The paper labels the increased ALFF region as 'Midbrain_L' with Brodmann Area 30 (BA30). BA30 is typically assigned to the retrosplenial cortex/parahippocampal area rather than the midbrain proper. This discrepancy is present in the paper itself; extracted verbatim without correction.
The paper does not report a PMID. The DOI is 10.1002/brb3.2057.
No trial registration number is reported in the paper.
